title: A database file and a table

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js opens data/kilnworth.db and prints the workshops it holds.

tasks.title: Create the workshops table
tasks.description:
Implement `createTables(db)` in `src/db.js`. It makes a table called `workshops` with these columns:

- `id`, the `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`
- `title` and `day`, text
- `seats` and `priceCents`, whole numbers

None of `title`, `day`, `seats` and `priceCents` may be left empty (`NULL`). When the table is already there, `createTables` leaves it and its rows as they are.

The check runs it on an empty database, looks at the columns it made, adds a row without an id and one without a title, and runs it a second time.
nextSteps: Write the `CREATE TABLE` statement with its five columns.
Mark the primary key and the columns that cannot be empty.
Make it safe to run when the table already exists.
hints: The column names are the same as the fields of a workshop in `src/workshops.js`.
Whole numbers are `INTEGER` and text is `TEXT`. `NOT NULL` after a column refuses a row without that value. `IF NOT EXISTS` after `CREATE TABLE` makes a second run do nothing.
`db.exec(`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workshops (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title TEXT NOT NULL, ...)`)`, with the other three columns in the same shape.

tasks.title: Fill the table once
tasks.description:
Implement `seedWorkshops(db, workshops)` in `src/db.js`. When the `workshops` table has no rows, it adds every workshop in the list it is given, each with its own `id`, `title`, `day`, `seats` and `priceCents`. When the table already has any row, it adds nothing.

Every value reaches the database apart from the SQL text, in the place of a `?`.

The check gives it workshops of its own on an empty table, calls it again, removes one workshop and calls it a third time. It also reads the SQL your function hands the database.
nextSteps: Count the rows the table has, and stop when there are any.
Prepare one `INSERT` with a `?` for each column.
Run it once for each workshop, with that workshop's values.
hints: A restart must not bring back a workshop the desk removed, so the only safe time to add the list is when the table is empty.
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS count FROM workshops` with `.get()` gives back `{ count }`. A prepared statement can run many times, each time with new values.
`const insert = db.prepare('INSERT INTO workshops (id, title, day, seats, priceCents) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)')`, then `insert.run(w.id, w.title, w.day, w.seats, w.priceCents)` for each workshop.

tasks.title: Open the database file
tasks.description:
Implement `openDatabase(file)` in `src/db.js`. It:

- makes the folder `file` goes in, when it is not there yet
- opens `file` as a SQLite database
- runs `createTables`, then `seedWorkshops` with the studio's `workshops` from `src/workshops.js`
- returns the open database

The check opens a file in a folder that does not exist yet, changes two workshops, closes it and opens the same file again, as a server restart would. It judges this task once the first two pass.
nextSteps: Set it up with the two functions you wrote, and return it.
hints: SQLite makes a database file that is missing, but it cannot make the folder around it.

`dirname(file)` from `node:path` is the folder of a path, and `mkdirSync(folder, { recursive: true })` from `node:fs` makes it and does nothing when it is there. `new DatabaseSync(file)` opens the file.
`mkdirSync(dirname(file), { recursive: true })`, then `const db = new DatabaseSync(file)`, `createTables(db)`, `seedWorkshops(db, workshops)` and `return db`.
